basis: Partial degeneration of the optic nerve; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis.
Congenital cardiac malformation involving ventricular outflow anatomy and a ventricular septal defect.
Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder; anemia occurs in 4/13 (~31%), just meeting the involvement threshold.
Lens displacement, cataracts and retinal dystrophy define this ocular syndrome.
Infection causes inflammation of the anterior uvea.
Progressive proximal skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiac and respiratory impairment are subtype-dependent, not established across most of the group.
Retinal degeneration and progressive sensorineural hearing loss define this Usher subtype and occur throughout the reported series.
Primary carcinoma of the uterine endometrium; reproductive organs have no axis.
Inherited marrow disorder characterized by monosomy 7, myelodysplasia and leukemia; no additional organ involvement is established.
Open spinal neural tissue malformation with a defining defect of the posterior vertebral arches.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis.
Inherited retinal disease; the definition establishes no extraocular disorder.
Adhesive scarring of the spinal arachnoid damages spinal roots and cord; infection or autoimmunity is not inherent to this diagnosis.
Displacement of the eyeball from its normal orbital position.
Calculus located in the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
Ectopic endometrial tissue directly occupies and affects the intestine.
Disordered intestinal secretion and absorption define the disease; electrolyte abnormalities are possible consequences, not defining metabolic disease.
Immune dysregulation with defining autoimmune cytopenias; hemolysis ~33% and thrombocytopenia 30%; nephritis 20% and thyroiditis 10% fall below threshold.
Primary mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the lung and bronchial airways.
Localized benign smooth muscle tumor of the orbit, arising from orbital vessel walls.
Clonal proliferation of blood-forming cells; later hematologic malignancy and cardiovascular disease are risks, not current additional organ damage.
Purely psychiatric impulse control disorder without defining structural or functional disease of an organ axis.
Benign or malignant neoplasm located in the rectum; lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Hemolysis, low platelets and hepatic injury define HELLP; hypertensive vascular involvement occurs in ~80%; AKI is rare and proteinuria alone is insufficient.
Defining skeletal and joint anomalies accompany lip and intraoral mucosal thickening; intellectual disability is reported in only 1/5 (20%).
